channel.title: MeltPet — Melting Hearts, One Pet at a Time
channel.description: Breed finder, cost calculators, and honest pet guides — researched by a team with combined experience in pet food, clinical research, and veterinary science. No AI fluff, no sponsored picks.

item.title: How to Start Raw Feeding a Dog Safely: 80/10/5/5 Explained
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Raw isn't "just meat." A pet food insider's safe-start playbook: the 80/10/5/5 nutrient map, a worked 340g example for a 30 lb dog, a 7-day transition, the four mistakes that send dogs to the ER, and honest bacteria risk management.

item.title: Cat Food Carbohydrate Calculator: Dry Matter Basis
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Most cat food labels don't list carbs. Enter the guaranteed analysis (protein, fat, fiber, ash, moisture) and see the real carbohydrate % on a dry matter basis — compare dry vs wet food fairly, and flag high-carb cat food.

item.title: Raw Dog & Cat Food Calculator: 80/10/10 Recipe Builder
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Build a balanced raw diet for your dog or cat. Prey Model Raw (PMR) ratio — 80% muscle meat, 10% edible bone, 5% liver, 5% other organ — calculated to the gram for your pet's weight and life stage, plus supplement doses.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Eat Poop? 1 in 6 Dogs Does It — The Paradox Study
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: One in six dogs eats poop. It is usually not a nutrient deficiency — it is a leftover wolf instinct. The 2018 UC Davis "paradox of coprophagy" study, why "greedy eaters" are the ones who do it, and the adult-onset red flag most articles skip.

item.title: Dog Weight Calculator: Is Your Dog Overweight? BCS Checker
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 60% of dogs are overweight and 40% of owners with overweight dogs think their dog is at a healthy weight. Breed-specific ideal weight ranges, Body Condition Score (BCS) visual guide, and a calorie-adjustment plan your vet would recommend.

item.title: Cat Calorie Calculator: RER + DER Formula, Real Portions
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: How many calories does your cat actually need? RER formula, activity multiplier, and the answer in real portions —cans of wet food, cups of kibble, or a mixed-feeding plan. The feeding guide on the bag is wrong —here's the real math.

item.title: Cat Dental Care Guide: Tooth Resorption, Stomatitis & the Kidney Connection
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 70% of cats have dental disease by age 3. Not the kind brushing fixes —the kind where the tooth eats itself from the inside while your cat purrs through it. Tooth resorption, stomatitis, and why your cat's mouth is connected to its kidneys.

item.title: British Shorthair Complete Guide: The Teddy Bear Cat That Doesn't Want to Be Held
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The cat that looks like a plush toy, feels like a warm brick, and has a personal-space policy stricter than an airline. HCM and PKD risks, the famous 'four-on-the-floor' rule, and what 15 years with a British Shorthair actually costs.

item.title: Pembroke Welsh Corgi Guide: Back Risks, Herding Drive & Real Costs (2026)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The Queen owned 30 of them. She also had staff to walk them. IVDD and DM risks, herding drive, the barking, and why this 30-pound dog thinks it's a German Shepherd. Full breed reality check.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Follow Me to the Bathroom? The Territory Theory
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your cat doesn't follow you to the bathroom because she loves you. She follows you because bathrooms are the most territorially interesting room in the house — warm, enclosed, full of surfaces, and usually inaccessible. The paw under the door isn't affection. It's a security audit.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Howl? It's Not a Wolf Call — It's Closer to Home
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Sirens, harmonicas, silence, or pure instinct. The real reasons dogs howl aren't about wolves — they're about acoustic biology, breed history, and who your dog thinks is in her pack.

item.title: Golden Retriever vs Labrador Retriever: Which One Is Right for Your Actual Life?
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: They look the same to non-dog-people. They're not the same dog. A head-to-head comparison of temperament, cost, health, and exercise — and a decision framework for which retriever actually fits your household.

item.title: Poodle Complete Guide: Three Sizes, Three Completely Different Dogs
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Toy, Miniature, or Standard — same breed name, radically different ownership experiences. Real costs by size, the grooming nobody warns you about, the intelligence that backfires on under-prepared owners, and how to pick the right Poodle for your life.

item.title: Why Do Cats Love Boxes? It's Not Just Hiding — It's Thermodynamics, Cortisol, and Ambush Math
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The box isn't just a hiding spot. It's a thermodynamic microclimate, a stress-reduction chamber, and the closest thing to an ambush position your living room can provide. Utrecht University shelter research, thermal imaging data, and the neuroscience of how a flimsy cardboard rectangle becomes the safest place in the house.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Sleep on Me? It's Not Just Warmth — It's Trust
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Sleeping is the most dangerous thing a cat does. When she chooses you as the place to be unconscious, it's the highest compliment in the feline vocabulary — higher than head-butting, higher than slow-blinking, higher than kneading. Body position meanings, purr frequency science, breed differences, and what to do when you're trapped.

item.title: 16 Hours a Day, and She's Still Tired. The Real Reason Your Cat Sleeps So Much
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your cat sleeps 12–18 hours a day. That's not laziness. Polyphasic sleep architecture, predator metabolic math, REM-to-light-sleep ratios by breed, and how to tell normal feline rest from pathological lethargy before it's too late.

item.title: Why Does My Dog Lick My Feet? It's Not the Salt — It's the Signal
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Every article says dogs lick feet for the salt. That's maybe 10% of the story. The real driver is your vomeronasal organ — dogs are reading your chemical biography through 250,000 sweat glands. Breed-by-breed breakdown, the 3-question compulsive vs. normal test, and how to redirect without making it worse.

item.title: Sphynx Cat Complete Guide: The Naked Truth About the Hairless Breed
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: No fur doesn't mean no maintenance. The Sphynx needs weekly baths, fleece sweaters, and a heated bed. Full guide to HCM screening, skin care, and why these cats are the ultimate lap-seeking missiles.

item.title: Dachshund Complete Guide: The Long Dog with the Fragile Spine
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 1 in 4 Dachshunds will develop IVDD. Ramps, weight management, and the right harness make the difference. Complete guide: temperament, cost, and the spine protection protocol every owner needs.

item.title: Cat Vomiting Color Guide: What Every Shade Means (White Foam to Blood Red)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Yellow bile, white foam, brown liquid, bright red blood — each color tells a different story. A vet-reviewed diagnostic tool with 12 vomit types, symptoms, and when to rush to the emergency clinic.

item.title: Cat Kidney Disease Prevention: What to Do Before the Creatinine Rises
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: CKD affects 30% of cats over 10. But it starts years before symptoms show. Hydration strategies, SDMA screening timelines, wet food benefits, and phosphorus control — the prevention protocol.

item.title: DIY Dog Grooming vs Professional: The Real Cost, Breed by Breed
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: A $40 clipper and a dream vs. an $85 groomer who spots ear infections before you do. Breed-by-breed breakdown: who you can DIY, who you absolutely shouldn't, and the hybrid approach that saves $400+/year.

item.title: Best Cat Litter Comparison: Clumping, Crystal, Clay, Natural — What Actually Works
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 6 litters tested. 4 weeks. 2 cats. Odor control, clumping strength, dust levels, and the one that handles high-volume CKD pee without turning to sludge.

item.title: Best Indestructible Dog Toys: 12 Toys That Survive Power Chewers (Tested)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Kong, Goughnuts, Benebone, and 9 others tested against a 90 lb German Shepherd. Which toys lasted 6 months, which ones died in 6 minutes, and why the wrong toy costs you $4,000 in foreign-body surgery.

item.title: First Year Dog Cost: The Real $5,237 Receipt
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Not the $1,500 the internet quotes. Real tracked expenses: supplies, vet visits, food, insurance, and the emergency fund. Every receipt, every surprise, every line item.

item.title: 17 Hidden Costs of Dog Ownership Nobody Warns You About
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Emergency boarding. Allergy shots. Destroyed drywall. Foreign-body surgery. The line items most calculators skip — from someone who tracked every dollar for 5 years.

item.title: Adopt vs Buy: The Full Cost, Health, and Temperament Breakdown
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: "Adopt don't shop" is a good slogan. It's also incomplete. The real cost, health, and temperament trade-offs — from someone who's worked with breeders, rescues, and overwhelmed first-time owners.

item.title: Is Pet Insurance Worth It in 2026? Five Real Scenarios Do the Math
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: $50/month premium × 12 years = $7,200. One TPLO surgery = $5,000. One cancer diagnosis = $15,000. Five real claim scenarios — and the breeds where insurance is mathematically a bargain.

item.title: New Kitten Checklist: What You Actually Need (Skip the $300 Bed)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The pet store wants you to buy everything. Your kitten needs about half. Litter box math (N+1 rule), the one toy they'll actually play with, and the supplies that prevent disaster in week one.

item.title: New Puppy Checklist: Survival Gear for the First 7 Days
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Crate, enzyme cleaner, a Kong that survives teething, and 11 other things you actually need. Not the $80 orthopedic bed your puppy will shred on night two.

item.title: Best Dog Food: Dry vs Wet vs Raw — An Industry Insider's Comparison
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 5 years in pet food taught me: most of what's on the bag is marketing. How to read a guaranteed analysis, why "human-grade" is unregulated, and the three-question filter that cuts through the noise.

item.title: New Tool: Dog Food Cost Calculator — Monthly Budget by Weight & Food Type
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Select your dog's weight and food type — kibble, wet, raw, or mixed. Instant monthly and annual cost estimates. See how switching from premium wet to high-quality kibble changes the number.

item.title: New Tool: Pet Compatibility Quiz — Dog or Cat: Which Pet Fits Your Life?
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 6 questions. 60 seconds. Dog person or cat person — the quiz doesn't ask what you want, it asks what your lifestyle can actually support. Workspace, activity level, travel schedule, and noise tolerance.

item.title: New Tool: Toxic Food Checker — 60+ Foods, Instant Safety Answer
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Can my dog eat grapes? Chocolate? Onions? Search 60+ foods instantly. Each entry: safety rating, toxic dose, symptoms timeline, and exactly what to do if your pet ate it.

item.title: New Tool: Pet Age Calculator — Dog & Cat Years to Human Years
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Convert your dog or cat's age to human years — using the real veterinary formula, not the 'multiply by 7' myth. Separate calculations by size: small, medium, large, and giant breeds age at different rates.

item.title: New Tool: Pet Name Generator — Thousands of Dog & Cat Names by Theme
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Browse thousands of pet names organized by theme: food, nature, funny, classic, human names, and myth & legend. One-click generation for dogs and cats. Find the one that sticks.

item.title: 3AM, Full Speed, No Warning: What Your Cat's Midnight Meltdown Actually Means
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your cat treating 2AM like an Olympic qualifier isn't random chaos — it's million-year-old crepuscular software running on apartment hardware. The biology behind the zoomies and five things that actually help you sleep.

item.title: Why Do Cats Knock Things Off Tables? It's Not Revenge — It's Physics Class
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your cat isn't being a jerk. It's running a physics experiment with its paw pads as sensors. The predator brain logic behind the behavior and three ways to redirect it.

item.title: Bengal Cat Complete Guide: The Leopard That Lives in Your Living Room
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Wild ancestry meets house cat. Bengals need wall shelves, puzzle feeders, and an owner who understands that "high energy" means 2 hours of active play daily. Full guide: cost, temperament, and the reality check.

item.title: Ragdoll Cat Complete Guide: The Floppy, Affectionate Lap Cat
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: They go limp when you pick them up. They follow you room to room. They're basically dogs in cat bodies. Full guide to the Ragdoll personality, cost, and why they're the ultimate family cat.

item.title: Why Does My Dog Stare at Me? The Real Science Behind the Canine Gaze
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your dog's stare isn't just love —it's a highly evolved operational tool. From the oxytocin bonding loop and predictive analytics to social referencing and medical warning signs, here's the full breakdown of why dogs lock eyes with humans —and how to read the nuance behind every gaze.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Wag Their Tails? Left vs. Right Wags Mean Different Things
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Neuroscientists have decoded the tail. Right-biased wag = positive (owner, friend). Left-biased = negative (unfamiliar dog, threat). The asymmetry is real, it's measurable, and knowing it makes you a better owner.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Roll in Smelly Things? Ancestral Scent Camouflage
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Dead worm perfume. Rotten fish cologne. Your dog isn't gross — it's running 40-million-year-old wolf software. The evolutionary biology of scent rolling and how to stop it without ruining the walk.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Follow You Everywhere? The Velcro Dog Phenomenon
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Even the bathroom. Every. Single. Time. It's not separation anxiety — it's 15,000 years of co-evolution. Your dog is studying your schedule, your habits, and your emotional state with 220 million scent receptors.

item.title: Why Do Dogs Eat Grass? It's Not What Your Grandma Said
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: They're not sick. They're not nutrient-deficient. A 2008 study surveyed 1,500+ dogs and found only 22% vomited after eating grass. The real answer involves ancestral wolf diets and a behavior called 'grazing.'

item.title: Why Does My Cat Knead Me? Blind Newborns, Scent Glands, and Ancient Lions
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: My tabby Gus has done this since day one. Most cats knead. Few owners know why. The answer involves blind newborn kittens, ancestral lions, and scent glands in their paw pads.

item.title: Summer Dog Safety: Hot Pavement, Heatstroke, and the 5-Second Rule That Saves Paws
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 77°F air = 125°F asphalt. At 87°F, the pavement hits 143°F — hot enough to burn paw pads in 60 seconds. Heatstroke kills in 15 minutes. Prevention protocol, early warning signs, and emergency first aid.

item.title: Calm a Dog During Fireworks: The Safe Room Protocol
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: July 4th sends more dogs to shelters than any other day. The desensitization timeline, the safe room setup, and the one medication protocol that works when training runs out of time.

item.title: Australian Shepherd Complete Guide: The Genius That Needs a Job
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Smartest dog you'll ever own. Also the most destructive if bored. Before you bring one home: the real exercise requirements, the herding behavior you can't train out, and why a tired Aussie is a good Aussie.

item.title: Maine Coon Complete Guide: The 20-Pound Gentle Giant
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: They play fetch. They love water. They chirp instead of meow. The Maine Coon is the most dog-like cat breed — and also one of the most expensive to own. Full cost breakdown, HCM screening, and grooming.

item.title: Labrador Retriever Complete Guide: America's Favorite Dog — At a Cost
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Labs eat everything. Socks. Rocks. The remote. The obesity stats are alarming, the joint problems are expensive, and that "easy" temperament needs 90 minutes of exercise daily. The truth about America's #1 breed.

item.title: German Shepherd Complete Guide: The Loyal Protector with the Fragile Hips
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Brilliant, loyal, and a hip dysplasia rate that should concern every potential owner. Full guide: temperament, working-line vs show-line differences, and the joint care protocol that starts on day one.

item.title: French Bulldog Complete Guide: The $5,000 Potato with a Spine Problem
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The most popular dog in America. Also a $5,000 purchase price with $10,000 in predictable vet bills. IVDD, BOAS, allergies — the health realities behind the bat ears. What every prospective Frenchie owner needs to know.

item.title: Dog Park Etiquette: 12 Unwritten Rules Every Owner Should Know
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Don't bring treats. Don't pick up your small dog. Don't stand still in the middle. The norms nobody tells first-timers — and the three behaviors that get you quietly banned from the park.

item.title: Separation Anxiety in Dogs: The Step-by-Step Desensitization Protocol
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Destruction, barking, and accidents when you leave aren't spite — they're panic. The clinical desensitization protocol from a veterinary behaviorist: departure cues, threshold training, and the 30-second foundation.

item.title: Leash Training: Stop Your Dog Pulling in 7 Days (Tree Method + U-Turn Method)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Two no-gimmick training protocols. No prong collars, no shock collars, no "be the alpha." Just the tree method for puppies and the U-turn method for adult pullers. Both work in about a week.

item.title: How to Stop Excessive Dog Barking: Fix the Root Cause, Not the Symptom
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Barking is a symptom. The cause is usually one of five things: boredom, anxiety, territoriality, greeting excitement, or learned attention-seeking. Diagnose the type first, then apply the right protocol.

item.title: How to Clean a Dog's Ears: Infection vs. Wax, What to Use, What Not to Use
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Flop-eared dogs need weekly cleaning. Pointy-eared dogs, monthly. The difference between normal wax and infection, the one solution you should never put in a dog's ear, and the cotton-ball trick vets teach.

item.title: Dog Dental Care: The Guide Your Vet Wishes You'd Read
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 80% of dogs have periodontal disease by age 3. A $500-1,000 dental cleaning under anesthesia vs. the $5 toothbrush routine. The toothbrushing desensitization protocol that takes 2 weeks.

item.title: Why Does My Dog Tilt Its Head? The Science of the Cutest Canine Behavior
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: My neighbor's Collie tilts so hard his whole body leans. A 2021 study finally explained why. It involves snout geometry, sound triangulation, and your dog actively studying your face.

item.title: Golden Retriever Complete Guide: The Family Dog with a 60% Cancer Rate
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: I love Goldens. I've also seen them returned to rescues. Before you bring one home: the real temperament, the real costs, and the 60% cancer rate nobody talks about.

item.title: How Much Does a Dog Cost Per Month? (2026 Real Numbers)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Small dog: $95–100. Medium: $145–190. Large: $210–320. Every line item explained with industry-sourced data and veterinary cross-referencing. Including the hidden costs most guides skip.

item.title: Why Does My Cat Bite Me Gently? It's Not Aggression — It's a Conversation
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: Your cat bites you softly, then licks the spot. It's not a warning — it's communication. Here's what the science says about love bites, overstimulation, and when to worry.

item.title: Maine Coon vs Ragdoll: The Big-Cat Showdown You Actually Need
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: 22 pounds of lynx energy, or a soft shadow that goes limp in your arms? Same size class, completely different roommates — size, grooming, health risks, and real costs compared.

item.title: How to Introduce a New Cat to Your Resident Cat (Step-by-Step)
item.dc:creator: Sarah Mitchell
item.description: The scent-first method that prevents hissing, hiding, and litter box wars. A realistic day-by-day timeline for cat introductions that actually work.
